PR #634 (Entire change #242), worktree /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/wp-onboarding-friction-fix (HEAD 6dfdc9f53, local, not pushed; remote is e987cc9b1). Trail #487. Read Codex's closure handoff first: /tmp/callisto-entire-242-246-2026-11-25/claude-closure-handoff.txt ('Correction A' and 'Protected decisions'). Two changes, nothing else: (1) git revert 4e4b8a178 (signed): 'no new JSON field for nothing-to-release hints' is a protected decision; the hint stays on stderr. (2) ce391643b renamed SeverityInference::requires_full_history to reads_history and used it to mean 'inference disabled'. Restore requires_full_history with its original meaning, and add a separate method on the same trait, fn is_active(&self) -> bool { true }, with NoInference returning false; gate the inference-only preparation in aggregate.rs (resolve_since, the window spec and the infer call) on is_active(), and keep the full-history check on requires_full_history(). Oracle per the handoff: disabled inference makes no inference-specific since/window/adapter calls; an injected inference-only failure does not affect the advisory; an enabled inference that needs no full history still runs; normal enabled inference keeps its shallow-clone error. Write unit tests with small test adapters for those four. Keep 6dfdc9f53's batching. Then the full gate by exit code (just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test, network unsandboxed, just fuzz-check, just bench and report the git process counts), then git fetch origin main && codex review --base origin/main; fix every actionable finding that does not contradict a protected decision (report any that does, e.g. if it asks for the JSON field again, instead of acting), re-run the gate, repeat until codex reports nothing actionable. Commit locally (signed) after each green gate. Report the final sha, each codex round's result and gate exit codes. Do NOT push. Rules (from the lead session close-gap-for-alpha). Be thorough before a push: a push costs a paid review, so find problems locally first.
- Read AGENTS.md. Prefer a type or private constructor over a check; delete checks a type makes redundant; fix sibling call sites in the same PR.
- A check, preview, dry run or test must run on exactly the structure the real path executes (one shared graph or derivation, the real tool), never a projection, copy or re-implementation. When fixing a failing or flaky test, assert the measured behaviour still happens.
- No new traits, async or frameworks. No new error codes, JSON keys or flags without asking the lead.
- Work in a named worktree off fresh origin/main. Write the failing test first for behaviour changes.
- Before reporting a change as ready to push, run the AGENTS.md gate in full and judge each by exit code: `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test` (workspace-wide, not just the touched crate; tests elsewhere read scripts, specs and error registries). Run network/pty tests unsandboxed. Iterate with scoped `cargo test -p` while working.
- If you change a public signature in callisto-manifests or callisto-model, also run `just fuzz-check` (the fuzz crate is outside the workspace, so crate tests miss it).
- Run `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff` only for new decision logic, not for merges, renames, docs, CI or tests; never commit mutants.out*.
- Merges and conflict resolutions: resolve, run the touched crate's tests, push. Nothing else.
- Changeset (`cargo run -p callisto-cli -- add ...`) only for user-visible changes, written for users.
- Every push triggers a paid review. Before reporting, run the checklist in /Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/d58474bb/tmp/review-checklist.md against your full diff. Push once, only after the lead has read your diff and says push; for an existing PR, commit locally and report the worktree and sha first.
- Signed commits, no session trailer. Merge the latest origin/main right before pushing (no rebase, no force-push). Push with git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>, confirm with git ls-remote, link the given trail, open with entire trail ci-pr.
- Trails are semantic outcomes shared by many PRs. Never change a trail's title or description (no `entire trail update` on it, no `entire trail create` to rename it). Put PR-specific text in the PR body with `gh pr edit <n> --body-file`. Link your branch to the trail the lead named; if your work does not fit that trail's outcome, ask the lead instead of linking it anyway.
- If CI fails, fix that failure only. If Entire raises findings, fix only wrong results, broken recovery, security issues or checks that cannot fail; report the rest to the lead.
- Report to the lead (close-gap-for-alpha) in under 5 lines: PR, sha, what you ran.
- CARGO_BUILD_JOBS is cores/5; never run two cargo builds in one worktree.
- Findings: the lead writes a row in /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/plans/FINDINGS-LEDGER.md (class, owning boundary, codebase-wide sweep, fix level) before any fix is briefed. If you find a finding without a row, stop and ask the lead.
- Prompt UI is final: line-based lists (plain text + inquire single-line Text). Findings about the prompt library's own behaviour are dismissed with a documented limit; fix only behaviour Callisto owns. Never redesign the prompt UI in response to a finding.

Task: close the remaining defect classes in Callisto Entire changes242 and246 without reopening settled product decisions.

Read the accompanying report.txt and verification-results.txt first. This is a bounded correction, not a new CLI, prompt or release architecture project. Do not push, approve, merge or post review resolutions unless the owner separately authorizes that action. Do not expose private unfixed findings through public repository docs.

Source baseline:
-242: e987cc9b1dfd54b9d87c4fd40d5a61b4821c69ca, wp-onboarding-friction, GitHub634.
-246: 1e12b4eb8fe6ee8dfbdfd5e5ef7d66fad88bd451, wp-interactive-cli-compare, GitHub638. This supersedes ffb3ac8 and already corrects the three previously open findings.
-Sampled origin/main:39a70f3111cf9d9f0b78c0062278f2a3a8546ab2. Re-read actual current heads before editing; a moving-head review is stale by definition.
-Both changes belong to trail487. The goal is install/init/correct preview/generated workflow in<10minutes, excluding registry account setup and new features.

Ownership:
One implementer owns shared init reconciliation and final behavior. Independent reviewers own falsification/evidence, not concurrent edits to the same lifecycle. Each subtask must state files, invariant, counterexamples, protected decisions and verification oracle. Keep Cargo builds serial in each checkout. Read AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, matching architecture topics and ADR index.

Correction A,242 disabled inference:
-Trace release_decision::pending_version_work -> plan_version -> aggregate -> resolve_since -> TagIndex::commit_of.
-NoInference currently suppresses infer itself after the caller has prepared windows. Gate inference-only preparation at the caller using an explicit existing-seam activity distinction. Enabled history-light inference is distinct from disabled inference; do not overload requires_full_history=false.
-Keep the real planner for selected, private, fixed/linked and retained-prerelease semantics. Do not count raw changeset files or swallow planner errors.
-Modern Git2.54/2.56 has no nested-tag process growth. The supported2.20–2.43 output contract does: the labeled compatibility probe measured exactlyN extra Auto calls forN packages. Preserve this qualification.
-Oracle: disabled inference makes no inference-specific since/window/adapter calls; injected inference-only failures do not affect advisory planning. Enabled history-light inference still runs; normal enabled inference retains shallow errors. Matched Auto/Changeset legacy/modern controls must show zero extra disabled work, not necessarily constant total release calls.

Correction B,246 shared changeset representation:
-Current latest source correctly normalizes standaloneCR, invokes writer validation before review/confirmation and matches only InitWorkflowExists. Retain those fixes.
-Shared model writer accepts CR/LF names and only quotes ASCII boundary spaces, while its reader normalizes/splits lines and trims Unicode whitespace. add can exit0 then status reports parse/unknown-package and pending0.
-Reject CR/LF identities unsupported by the current line grammar. Quote all boundary whitespace the reader trims. Preserve quote rejection and exact identity; do not normalize names or duplicate registry grammars.
-Fix shared writer/quoting so every caller benefits. Keep model MIT dependencies downward, normal diagnostics, atomic writes and ApplyPermit.
-Oracle: for canonical summaries and distinct representable entries, parse(write(candidate)) preserves identities, severities and summary. Unsupported representation errors before review/confirmation/file creation. Include LF/CR, tabs, NBSP, space, quotes, colon/hash, scoped and ordinary names with positive controls. Exercise flags and wizard, real/dry-run, decline/cancel. Use bounded generated character classes if useful; do not claim exhaustive fuzz coverage.
-Serializing the same unchanged value twice through the same pure writer is not an established defect. A private PreparedChangeset carrying bytes is optional if it simplifies the code; do not make it a new requirement or introduce a framework.

Correction C,integrated init:
-The two current branches conflict in CLI commands/init.rs and its tests. Neither choosing ours/theirs wholesale nor testing each branch alone closes the pair.
-Keep242 Notes exactly-once diagnostics and246 prompt capability: Text +TTY stdin +TTY stderr; piped stdout allowed; JSON never prompts.
-Suppress workflow question only for proven Existing. For I/O failure: explicit --workflow/interactiveYes is fatal before config write; --no-workflow/interactiveNo can skip; unrequested automatic failure warns and continues. Existing owner bytes preserved.
-Test public mode and stream boundaries, plus success/decline/later error. Do not rely only on injected JSON+prompt unit states that the public capability now excludes.

Latest-review product-selector decision:
-New low01M8AG82P1GBPTZ84HWTDD0E5N is independently reproduced: wizard rejects bare tool but accepts displayed cargo/tool; --product-package tool succeeds. Both preserve selected cargo/tool identity; rejected answers reprompt without writes.
-Current documented picker accepts listed names and lists qualifiedIDs; no explicit bare-alias promise was found. Classify this as UX consistency work, not a proven security/correctness blocker or automatically added owner requirement.
-Recommended correction, if adopting consistency: reuse InitFacts::product_package qualified/unique-bare semantics at product selector boundary; keep IDs visible; exact-name priority and workspace ambiguity must match existing flag behavior. Test unique/ambiguous/qualified/numeric names; do not strip prefixes and take the first match or invent another token grammar.
-Alternatively preserve listed-ID-only policy with precise prompt wording and a recorded scope disposition. Do not silently treat a reviewer preference as a new gate.

Protected decisions:
-No remote transport/rewrite redesign here; reverted/deferred to trail494. No registry-destination authorization policy.
-No new JSON field for nothing-to-release hints. Keep stderr advice and actual planner's durable-path restrictions.
-Keep static full-name lists, Inquire text input and exact-name-first grammar; no #N or new renderer.
-Keep owner-approved externalSIGINT/editor behavior; do not resurrect signal threads or superseded restoration requirements.
-No new native auth broker, Tokio runtime, public adapter framework, Windows support gate or release Environment/reviewer gate.

Evidence process and stop rule:
-Reproduce before fixing. Run focused real-function/CLI tests for each complete boundary and affected siblings. An independent reviewer reviews the accumulated final diff, with counterexamples and negative controls, rather than only the last commit.
-Run required AGENTS gates after the final edit and just bench for Git-process behavior. Judge every check by exit code; retain full logs. Freeze final SHA before claiming completion.
-Record each existing finding with exact finalSHA, old reproduction, corrected invariant and passing oracle. A new suggestion must be classified as contract violation, hypothesis, or owner decision; never silently add the latter as a gate.
-Check final CI/review/approval state separately. Time the intended fresh-user walkthroughs separately from unit checks.
-Stop when there are no confirmed unresolved violations of the accepted contract, these matrices pass on the combined artifact and existing gates are satisfied. Do not promise there can never be another finding.

4e4b8a178 fix(release): the nothing-to-release report carries pending-version diagnostics
ce391643b fix(release): the changesets-only hint works out no inference window
e987cc9b1 fix(init): print the cancellation on stderr when a JSON-mode init is declined
9af0ce238 fix(release): build E120's shown registry from the validated binding instead of re-parsing the raw override
614cc2ae1 Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into worktree-wp-onboarding-friction-fix
d31a16da8 fix(init,release): keep a failed pending check off the init report; say the merge note before the next steps
87713316a fix(init,release): narrow the pending-hint claim; drop the repeated access warning on E342; list the failed pending check in init JSON; clearer E120 and tag outlook wording

content.content:
Pre-push self-review checklist (from recurring Entire reviewer findings). Check your full diff against every item; fix or justify each before reporting. Every push triggers a paid review: do not push until the lead says so.

1. Secrets: no user-supplied URL, remote, token, env value or path that may carry credentials is printed in any message, error, JSON or log. Print only values we derived ourselves (owner/repo slug, package names). Child processes get the runner's filtered environment.
2. Same structure for preview and real: dry runs, hints and previews compute on exactly the set/plan the real command uses (selection, group expansion, publishable packages, roster). No second derivation.
3. Modes: text vs --format json vs non-TTY. JSON stdout stays a single document; human notes go to stderr once in both modes; json never prompts. Check every new message in all three modes.
4. Validation order: mode/eligibility first, then input validation, then prompts or side effects. A bad input never reaches a confirmation screen.
5. Optional conveniences (preselection, detection, previews, hints) degrade with a warning; they never make the command fail.
6. Never parse text we rendered, and never hand-parse a foreign grammar (Markdown, git URLs, shell) beyond the coarse classification we need; prefer the owning tool or omit.
7. Rust: exhaustive match on our own enums (no _ arm); no unwrap outside tests; expect names its invariant; no swallowed errors (.ok(), drop(result)) without a one-line reason; no process::exit outside main; Drop-based cleanup; no global mutable state unless unavoidable; minimal visibility.
8. Edge inputs for anything touching user paths or strings: spaces, newlines, leading ':' or '-', unicode, empty, very long.
9. Tests: one test per behaviour through the real binary where users see it; tests clean up children and temp files on failure.
11. Consumers: for every function, field, type or enum variant whose behaviour or meaning you changed, list every reader (rg the name across crates, including the changelog, version planner, release preview, PR body, JSON reports and tests) and confirm each still gets what it expects. A value with two jobs must be split, not repurposed.
10. Precedent: when a behaviour has a well-known precedent (git, cargo, npm, changesets), follow it and cite it rather than inventing.

content.text:
The gate (pre-push, lint, doc-check, test, fuzz-check) is still running in the background; I'll pick up when it finishes.

Where things stand:
- **Revert:** `4e4b8a178` (the nothing-to-release JSON field) is reverted as `13a4ab2ef`. The commit is signed (`G`).
- **Trait split:** `requires_full_history()` is back with its original meaning. I added `is_active()`, which defaults to `true`; `NoInference` returns `false` for both.
- **Gate in `aggregate.rs`:**
  - `is_active()` now gates the inference-only preparation: `resolve_since`, the inputs the window needs (`pathspecs`, `policy`), the window spec and the `infer` call.
  - The full-history check still uses `requires_full_history()`.
- **Tests:** four new unit tests in `aggregate/tests.rs`, all passing. They use a git runner that records calls and can inject failures, a configurable inference adapter, and a real repo whose release tag points at another tag, so working out the window has to ask git.
  - Disabled inference: no `^{commit}` peel, no shallow check, no `infer` call, even with all three set to fail; the pending changeset still plans a patch bump.
  - Enabled inference that needs no full history still runs, and gets the peeled tag's commit as `since`.
  - Normal enabled inference in a real `--depth 1` clone still fails with `ShallowHistory`.
  - A small fourth test checks that `NoInference` reports itself as inactive and needing no history.
  - Negative controls: with the `is_active` gate removed, the disabled-inference test fails; with the full-history check removed, the shallow-clone test fails.
- **Checklist item 11 (consumers):** the only production caller of `NoInference` is `release_decision.rs:169` (the pending hint), so nothing else changes behaviour.

Still to do: `just bench` with git process counts, the signed local commit, then `codex review --base origin/main` rounds. Nothing has been pushed.
